title: Greco-Persian Wars
summary: The Greco-Persian Wars grew out of the Ionian rebellion against Persian rule and the attack on Sardis in 499 BCE. Persian forces sent by Darius I and later Xerxes I invaded mainland Greece, and the wars' famous battles were fought at Marathon, Thermopylae, Salamis and Plataea. The Greeks were ultimately victorious and formed the Delian League to ward off further attacks. A peace, sometimes called the Peace of Callias, followed around 449 BCE.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia dates the wars from the Ionian Revolt (499 BCE) through the Peace of Callias in c. 449 BCE; UNESCO links Athenian classical emergence to 5th-century BC victory over the Persians.

where.historical_name: Athens and allied Greek poleis confronting the Achaemenid Persian Empire

importance.justification: Greek victory kept the mainland city-states free of Persian rule at the start of the classical age.
